intro.header: Representing Inequalities on a Number Line
intro.objective: Show the solution set of an inequality on a number line using open and filled circles and arrows, and read an inequality from a given number line.
commonMistakes: Using a filled circle for < or > — these need an OPEN circle (value not included).
Using an open circle for ≤ or ≥ — these need a FILLED circle (value included).
Drawing the arrow the wrong way: it points towards the values that make the inequality true.
Forgetting to rearrange first, e.g. −2 ≤ x is the same as x ≥ −2.
methodSteps: Step 1: Find the boundary value (the number in the inequality).
Step 2: Choose the circle — open ○ for < or >, filled ● for ≤ or ≥.
Step 3: Draw an arrow towards the values that satisfy the inequality (left for </≤, right for >/≥).
Step 4: For a 'between' inequality, mark both ends and shade in between.
Step 5: To read a line, reverse the process: circle type gives < / ≤, direction gives the rest.
workedExample: Step 2 — ≥ means −2 is included, so use a FILLED circle ●.
Step 3 — 'Greater than or equal to' points right, so the arrow goes right.
Step 5 — Read-back check: filled circle at −2 with arrow right = x ≥ −2 ✓

frame: Open circle ○ for > (the value is not included).
The arrow points right for 'greater than'.
questions.content:
Show each inequality on a number line.

   a) x > 1
   b) x ≤ 4

frame: ≥ means the value IS included, so use a filled circle ●.
Negative numbers go to the left of zero.
questions.content:
Show each inequality on a number line.

   a) x ≥ −3
   b) x < 0

Write the inequality shown by each number line.

   a) An open circle at 2 with the arrow pointing right.
   b) A filled circle at −1 with the arrow pointing left.

Show each inequality on a number line.

   a) x ≥ 5
   b) x < −4
   c) −2 ≤ x

Solve each inequality, then show the solution on a number line.

   a) 2x + 1 > 7
   b) 3x − 2 ≤ 10
   c) 5 − 2x ≥ 1

Write an inequality for each statement and show it on a number line.

   a) The number n is at least −1.
   b) The temperature t (°C) is below 5.

A number line has a filled circle at −3, an open circle at 4, and the section between them shaded.

   a) Write the inequality shown. (1 mark)
   b) List all the integers that satisfy it. (2 marks)

A machine only works safely when the temperature t (°C) is both at least 10 and below 35.

   a) Write each condition as an inequality and show each on a number line. (2 marks)
   b) Write the two conditions as one combined inequality. (1 mark)
   c) The temperature is exactly 35 °C. Is the machine safe? Explain your answer. (2 marks)

answers.title: Teacher key
rows: Q1: a) open circle ○ at 1, arrow right  b) filled circle ● at 4, arrow left
Q2: a) filled circle ● at −3, arrow right  b) open circle ○ at 0, arrow left
Q4: a) filled ● at 5, arrow right  b) open ○ at −4, arrow left  c) −2 ≤ x means x ≥ −2: filled ● at −2, arrow right
Q5: a) 2x > 6 → x > 3 (open at 3, right)  b) 3x ≤ 12 → x ≤ 4 (filled at 4, left)  c) −2x ≥ −4 → x ≤ 2 (filled at 2, left)
Q6: a) n ≥ −1 (filled ● at −1, arrow right)  b) t < 5 (open ○ at 5, arrow left)
Q8: a) t ≥ 10 (filled at 10, right) and t < 35 (open at 35, left)  b) 10 ≤ t < 35  c) Not safe — t < 35 means 35 is not included, so 35 °C is outside the safe range.
